subtitulo: Three answers and the booking does the rest
introPt: A traveller clears the border desk in four short answers.
cenario: The border desk, first hour after landing.

dialogo.es: こんにちは。旅行の目的は何ですか？
dialogo.pt: Hello. What is the purpose of your trip?
dialogo.tts: こんにちは。旅行の目的は何ですか？

dialogo.es: 東京の、ホテルです。はい、これです。
dialogo.pt: In Tokyo, in a hotel. Yes, here it is.
dialogo.tts: 東京の、ホテルです。はい、これです。

perguntas.pergunta: «Ryokou no mokuteki wa nan desu ka?» — what is being asked?
perguntas.explica: Mokuteki is the purpose. Duration and address are separate questions with separate answers.

opcoes: Hands over the document — 'here it is'
perguntas.explica: Three syllables and an open hand. It moves the exchange off your memory and onto your evidence.

perguntas.pergunta: The officer asks one short question. What is the best-shaped answer?
opcoes: The full itinerary, so nothing looks hidden
Only what was asked, then stop
perguntas.explica: The desk is working through matched pairs. An answer that runs past its question reads as material to check, not as warmth.

perguntas.pergunta: You did not catch what was said. What do you say?
perguntas.explica: Say it once, plainly. Guessing at a border desk costs more time than asking.

perguntas.pergunta: Why is «kankou desu» enough, rather than «kankou» alone?
opcoes: It is a rule of Japanese grammar that every noun needs it
The -desu ending is what keeps a one-word reply polite
perguntas.explica: Politeness rides on the -desu ending and a small nod, not on a longer sentence. Kankou alone is bare; kankou desu is complete and courteous.
